record.original_question: Beyond the known Reed–Muller cases, for which cyclic codes is the entire code generated by its minimum-weight codewords?

evidence.quote: This leads to the general problem: for which other cyclic codes does this property hold ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let $n$ be a positive integer with $\gcd(n,q)=1$. A linear code $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ is called cyclic if it is invariant under the cyclic shift $(c_0,c_1,\dots,c_{n-1}) \mapsto (c_{n-1},c_0,\dots,c_{n-2})$. Equivalently, via the identification $\mathbb{F}_q^n \cong \mathbb{F}_q[x]/(x^n-1)$, $C$ is an ideal in this quotient ring. The (Hamming) weight $\operatorname{wt}(c)$ of a codeword $c \in C$ is the number of nonzero coordinates, and the minimum distance is $d(C) = \min\{\operatorname{wt}(c) : c \in C,\ c \neq 0\}$. Let $M(C) \subseteq C$ denote the set of minimum-weight codewords of $C$, i.e., those with $\operatorname{wt}(c) = d(C)$.

It is known that binary Reed–Muller codes (which form a class of cyclic-extended codes) have the property that they are generated as $\mathbb{F}_q$-vector spaces by their minimum-weight codewords.

Problem: Characterize, beyond the Reed–Muller family, all cyclic codes $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ with the property that $C = \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{F}_q} M(C)$, i.e., $C$ is generated by its minimum-weight codewords.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization remains open. Recent work (e.g., a 2024 arXiv preprint on low-weight codewords in cyclic codes and 2025 work on BCH codes) continues to study minimum-weight codewords and bases of cyclic/BCH codes, indicating that the question of which cyclic codes are generated by their minimum-weight codewords is still actively studied without a complete answer.

status_evidence.title: Low-weight codewords in cyclic codes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies low-weight codewords in cyclic codes, including bases of small-weight codewords for BCH codes, motivating an explicit description of generating sets.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of describing generators by low/minimum weight codewords for general cyclic codes (beyond Reed–Muller) remains an active topic without complete resolution.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on cyclic codes
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists generation by minimum weight codewords as a general open problem for cyclic codes beyond Reed–Muller cases.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as open in standard coding-theory surveys.
